subject: Quality monitoring: implementation matrix, canary/rollback policies, and eval integration

Hi Stephanie and Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to start the staged rollout of the Hemera model variant for our clinical triage assistant, and we need help designing a quality monitoring implementation that covers: prompt sets, eval integration, regression alerts, and a canary + rollback policy. High-level constraints:

- Latency SLO: 350ms p95
- Traffic: starting at 5% of requests, ramp to 50% over two weeks
- Data sensitivity: PHI-ish (pseudonymized), retention needs to be controlled

Specific asks:
- A compact implementation matrix that maps owners, artifacts (prompt sets, evals), and alert thresholds
- Concrete canary metrics and rollback triggers we can plug into our runbook
- A short list of eval harness integration steps so our infra team can wire CI -> staging -> production checks

Can you sketch this out so we can align internal stakeholders (SRE, security, product) ahead of the kickoff? I've CC'd Arjun (ops) who will be doing the infra work.

Appreciate it — we want predictable, measurable rollback behavior rather than ad-hoc stops.

Best,
Samira Khan

Novamed

On Mon, Aug 18, 2025 at 11:08 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'm putting together a short implementation matrix and a recommended canary/rollback policy.

Thanks — adding technical specifics below so Novamed can hand these to SRE/infra. I'll upload short scripts to the Drive folder after this thread.

Eval harness integration (high level):
- Staging hook: push new model commit -> run unit evals (prompt set v1) -> produce metric bundle (accuracy proxies, refusal rate, hallucination score, avg token latency)
- Gate: staging must meet baseline thresholds (e.g., hallucination score <= 0.06, refusal rate <= 1.5%) before canary deploy
- Canary: deploy at 5% traffic for 48h, collect metrics, compare to baseline with rolling windows (1h/6h/24h)

Canary metrics (recommended):
- Functional: top-10 prompt accuracy, BLEU-ish signal for templated responses, critical-label false positive rate
- Safety/quality: hallucination_score (model-side heuristic), refusal_rate, PII-leak checks (regex-based sampling)
- Performance: p95 latency, token-per-response cost delta

Rollback triggers (automatable):
- Hard triggers (immediate rollback): any critical-label FP increase > 25% relative to baseline OR PII leak detected in sampled outputs
- Soft triggers (pause/rate limit + human review): hallucination_score increases > 40% OR p95 latency increase > 60% OR sustained drop in top-10 accuracy > 10% over a 6h window

Operational notes:
- Automate rollback via routing policy: traffic re-routed to previous model variant if hard trigger is hit; send automated incident to on-call + CS channel
- Keep a warm fallback variant for rapid switch (same quantization profile to avoid cold-start variability)
- KV/prefix cache: consider TTL on friendly prefixes to avoid stale cached completions during canary

I'll attach eval snippets and a simple Prometheus alert rule set.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — a few additions from ops/product side: please see inline.

- Canary duration: 48h is fine for initial; add a mandatory 72h stability check before moving past 25% traffic (we want two independent rolling windows)
- Canary dashboard: include 'regression-alert' synthetic that pins to 10 focused prompts (owner: Novamed CS)
- Incident playbook: map soft triggers to a Tier-2 review (CS + SE within 30m) and hard triggers to automatic rollback + Tier-1 pager (SRE)
- Ownership: Redwood will provide the alerting templates and a one-time runbook walkthrough. Novamed to own the final runbook in their internal ops repo.

I'd also recommend a pre-rollout QA dry run: run the eval harness on the current production model vs candidate for a smoke comparison to catch obvious regressions. Schedule that as a gating step in the implementation matrix.

Laura Bennett
Product Ops — Observability, Redwood Inference
